summary: Hungary's prosecutors publish each year how many offences of each type were committed by foreign citizens, including endangering a minor, child pornography, sexual violence and homicide. That is a citizenship proxy for perpetrators only; victims are published by age without citizenship, and the census's Roma and nationality data are never linked to crime or child-protection records.

nations.National (Prosecutor General, KSH, Inter: Annual prosecutor crime report; KSH offender and victim tables.

european_title: Not recorded by any Hungarian crime source
european_note: Hungarian crime statistics separate only foreign citizens from the rest. The census asks about nationality (nemzetiség), including Roma, but no crime, victim or child-protection statistic records it, so neither ethnic Europeans nor Roma identity can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Hungary records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity or nationality group. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual violence (registered offences, all victims)
harms.intro: Of 417 registered sexual violence offences in 2025, 17 were committed by foreign citizens. Sexual violence includes, but is not limited to, offences against children under 12 and 14. KSH counted 3,396 crime victims under 14 and 412 victims of sexual violence in 2025, with no citizenship.

victims.text: KSH and police victim tables give age and sex but no citizenship.

perpetrators.share_note: Prosecutor General's 2025 report: registered offences committed by foreign (non-Hungarian) citizens, against all registered offences of that type in 2025 (Table 11). The total includes offences whose perpetrator is not known, so the foreign share is a lower bound. Counts are offences, not persons, all victim ages. Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: foreign citizens are people without Hungarian citizenship (most often Romanian, Ukrainian, Slovak and Serbian citizens, many of them ethnic Hungarians); Hungarian citizens include Roma and every other nationality group.

cross.text: No victim data by citizenship, so nothing can be linked.

breakdown.why: The Prosecutor General's 2025 crime report gives registered sexual violence offences committed by foreign (non-Hungarian) citizens (17 of 417), all victim ages. KSH victim tables give age (3,396 victims under 14 in 2025) but no citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The prosecutor's report gives domestic (relationship) violence by foreign citizens (10 of 968 registered offences), all victim ages; no child victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Intentional completed homicide: 5 of 78 registered offences in 2025 by foreign citizens, all victim ages. KSH counts 96 homicide victims with no citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Trafficking and forced labour: 3 of 74 registered offences in 2025 by foreign citizens. No official count of trafficking victims by nationality was found. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child pornography: 10 of 731 registered offences in 2025 by foreign citizens. No victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Hungary scores 7% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. The Prosecutor General's annual crime report counts offences committed by foreign (non-Hungarian) citizens, including endangering a minor, child pornography, sexual violence and homicide; KSH gives offenders by citizenship but victims by age only. The census records Roma and other nationalities, but no crime, victim or child-protection statistic does.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.

ugy.name: Tájékoztató a bűnözés 2025. évi adatairól
ugy.publisher: Legfőbb Ügyészség (Office of the Prosecutor General of Hungary)
ugy.records: Registered offences by type; offences and offenders by foreign citizenship and the main foreign nationalities.
ugy.limitations: Hungarian/foreign citizenship only; offences not persons; no victim citizenship.

ksh.name: STADAT 11.1.1.4 Regisztrált elkövetők; 11.1.1.5 Regisztrált sértettek
ksh.records: Offenders by age, recidivism and Hungarian/foreign citizenship (5,721 foreign of 169,278 in 2025); victims by age and offence type.
ksh.limitations: Victims have no citizenship; offenders not by offence and citizenship together.

bsr.name: Bűnügyi Statisztikai Rendszer (BSR)
bsr.records: Interactive tables of offences, offenders and victims.
bsr.limitations: The report files are served from bsr-sp.bm.hu, which did not answer from the box; the portal says reports open only in Firefox. Not used.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
